question: Which of the following was first introduced in bacterial cells by the American molecular biologist Joshua Lederberg in 1952?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Joshua Lederberg, an American molecular biologist, first introduced the concept of **plasmids** in bacterial cells in 1952.
 
• A plasmid is a small, circular, double-stranded DNA molecule that is distinct from the chromosomal DNA and can replicate independently.
 
• Plasmids are primarily found in bacteria but can also exist in archaea and eukaryotic organisms under certain conditions.
 
• Lederberg's discovery played a crucial role in understanding bacterial genetics and paved the way for genetic engineering techniques.
 
• Plasmids are widely used in molecular biology as vectors to clone, transfer, and manipulate genes in research and biotechnology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmid Types:**

 
 
• **F-plasmids:** Responsible for bacterial conjugation, facilitating gene transfer between cells.
 
• **R-plasmids:** Carry antibiotic resistance genes, contributing to antimicrobial resistance.
 
• **Col-plasmids:** Encode bacteriocins, proteins that kill or inhibit other bacteria.
 
• **Degradative plasmids:** Allow bacteria to metabolize unusual substances like hydrocarbons.
 
 
 
• **Significance in Biotechnology:**
 
 
• Plasmids are used as **vectors** to introduce foreign DNA into host cells in genetic engineering.
 
• They are essential in producing recombinant proteins, such as insulin and vaccines.
 
 
 
• **Bacterial Conjugation:**
 
 
• It is a process where genetic material is transferred between bacterial cells via direct contact.
 
• Plasmids play a key role in this process, enhancing genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Plasmid Replication:**
 
 
• Plasmids replicate independently of chromosomal DNA, either through a rolling-circle mechanism or bidirectional replication.
 
• This property makes them suitable for laboratory manipulation and cloning experiments.
